# derived from Linux /proc semantics and DESIGN.md §7.1, not captured from a run
# Expectation for the doctor check `ports_owned` (DESIGN.md §7.1) against input/.
# How to read this file: tests/fixtures/doctor/node_layout/expect.json.
#
# THE CHECK READS EVERYTHING THROUGH paths.proc_root, WHICH IS WHY THIS FIXTURE CAN DRIVE IT AT ALL:
# §7.1 says ports_owned reads "<proc_root>/net/tcp, <proc_root>/*/fd" -- not the real /proc, and not
# `ss` or `lsof` (neither is guaranteed installed, the same reason §2i rejects lsof/fuser).
#
# input/proc/net/tcp IS A KERNEL-FORMAT SAMPLE, not a convenience format, and two columns bite:
#   local_address is HEX-IP:HEX-PORT with the IP in inet_addr byte order, so 127.0.0.1 prints as
#     0100007F and 0.0.0.0 as 00000000. A parser that reads it as big-endian dotted order sees
#     127.0.0.1 as 1.0.0.127 and the loopback test silently inverts.
#   the PORT IS HEX: 18080 = 0x46A0, 18081 = 0x46A1, 18083 = 0x46A3. Reading it as decimal finds
#     nothing and the check reports `pass` on every machine -- the vacuous-gate failure of §2j.
#   st = 0A is TCP_LISTEN; a fixture row with any other st is not a bound port.
#   the LAST column is the socket INODE, and that is the join key: /proc/<pid>/fd/<n> is a symlink to
#     `socket:[<inode>]`, so "who listens on this port" is (port -> inode) then (inode -> pid).
# input/proc/<pid>/fd/<n> ARE DANGLING SYMLINKS ON PURPOSE. git stores the link TARGET, which is the
#   only thing the scan reads; there is no socket to point at. A harness that copies the tree must
#   preserve symlinks (`cp -a`, not `cp -rL`, which would fail on a dangling link).
#
# THIS CASE: OUR OWN TWO UNITS own all three ports, all on 127.0.0.1.
#   18080 (P2P) and 18081 (RPC) -> inodes 5501/5502 -> pid 41233, which is fmonero-monerod.service's
#     MainPID in input/systemctl.txt
#   18083 (wallet RPC)          -> inode 5503        -> pid 51002, fmonero-wallet-rpc.service's MainPID
# §7.1: `pass` when the listener is our unit's PID or nothing. So the systemctl fixture is REQUIRED
# for this case -- without it there is no MainPID to compare against and the right answer would be
# `warn` (an unknown process) for all three rows.
# 18080 AND 18081 ARE THE PORTS §7.1 NAMES LITERALLY, plus wallet.port; 18083 is the default
# (DESIGN.md §4: 18082 is monerod's ZMQ port, so the wallet takes 18083).
# status `pass`; the detail should name what it found rather than only "ok", so that a run against an
# empty /proc -- which also yields `pass` under §7.1's "our unit's PID OR NOTHING" -- is
# distinguishable from this one.
